Thresholds settings

Declare monitoring limits once per product (and for SATOM and its host) so every probe that has no value of its own inherits them, with the origin of every number shown.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Monitoring & Alerts → Thresholds (URL /settings/#tab-thresholds)

What is it?#

Thresholds is the measurement policy: what a number has to reach before it is graded warning or critical. You declare a limit once per scope and every probe that has not been given its own value follows it live. Who is told, and how often, is delivery policy and lives on Email & Alerts.

What does it do?#

  • Offers one scope per product ADOM (from the ADOM registry — normally FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator), plus SATOM (the application) and SATOM host (the machine).
  • For a product scope, three sections:
  • Measurement — per probe kind that the product can run (only kinds the product supports are shown).
  • Device roll-up — how the device signals combine into the badge on Fleet health.
  • Binary facts — conditions with no number, each set to crit, warn or off (still shown, never graded).
  • For SATOM (the application) — six limits of the alert engine; they are the same stored values as the matching fields on Email & Alerts.
  • For SATOM host (the machine) — disk, memory and load of the node itself, graded on both HA nodes.
  • Each field shows set here or default N; facts show changed or default ….

Requirements#

  • users.manage.
  • Probes to grade (see Probes and Deep monitors).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

GET /settings/thresholds/state, POST /settings/thresholds and POST /settings/thresholds/reset require users.manage; others get 403 and do not see the tab.

How to use#

  1. Open Settings → Monitoring & Alerts → Thresholds. The panel loads when first opened.
  2. Click a scope button at the top.
  3. Type values. Leave a box empty to clear the override (the field falls back to the shipped default and every inheriting probe follows). Type 0 to switch that level off.
  4. Click Save this scope. The status line reads "Saved N, cleared M." or lists the errors.
  5. To undo everything in the scope, click Revert scope to shipped defaults and confirm "Clear every override in this scope and go back to the shipped defaults?" — "Cleared N override(s)."
  1. 1Probe columnused only if someone set a value on that probe
  2. 2Scope valuewhat you save on this tab
  3. 3Shipped defaultthe value in the product, never a crash

Configuration#

Product scope — Measurement (per probe kind)#

Field Kind Default Notes
Slow response https 2000 ms 0 disables.
Certificate expiry https 21 days Warn at this many days left.
Harvest age budget interface 6 h Older readings are reported stale.
CPU warning / CPU critical cpu 80 % / 95 % 0 disables.
Memory warning / Memory critical memory 80 % / 95 % 0 disables.
Concurrent sessions warning / critical sessions 0 / 0 Absolute count; nothing enabled by default.
Policy sessions warning / critical policy_sessions 0 / 0 Rarely fires on short-lived HTTP; 0 disables.
Application latency policy_sessions 2000 ms 0 disables.
Throughput warning / critical throughput 0 / 0 Mbps Graded on the peak of the window.
Transactions warning / critical transactions 0 / 0 0 disables.
Licence consumed warning / critical licence 80 / 95 % consumed 0 disables.
Token pool warning / critical tokens 80 / 95 % consumed 0 disables.

Product scope — Device roll-up#

Field Default Notes
Cache age budget 6 h Older cached configuration = warning. A legacy monitoring.stale_hours value is honoured below the scope value.
Critical multiplier 4 x Cache older than budget × this = critical.
Harvest failures before critical 3 runs One failure = warning.
Object capacity warning / critical 80 % / 95 % Types with no cap are reported unknown, never passing.

Product scope — Binary facts#

Fact Default
Every backend of a server policy is down crit
Some backends of a server policy are down warn
A pool member has no health check configured warn
Server policy is administratively disabled warn
Server policy membership changed warn
The proxy daemon is not running crit
The proxy daemon's PID set changed warn
A monitored interface changed IP or link state crit
A monitored interface vanished from the harvest crit
Transaction counter reads zero while the policy carries traffic warn

off changes the grade, never the visibility: the fact is still printed on the probe.

SATOM (the application)#

Field Default Shared with Email & Alerts field
Certificate expiry warning 14 days Cert warn (days)
Standby commits behind 25 commits Git behind max
Unpushed commit age 6 h Git unpushed max (hours)
Newest backup bundle age 48 h Backup stale (hours)
Scheduled action failures before critical 3 runs Automation fail streak → critical
Scheduled action overdue 3 h Automation overdue (hours)

The alert engine reads the three hour values as whole hours: a value saved here as 12.0 counts as 12, and a fraction is dropped (12.5 counts as 12).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: hour values saved on this tab (stored as decimals such as 12.0) are honoured by the alert engine; before, it could not read them and silently used its defaults.

SATOM host (the machine)#

Field Default
Filesystem used — warning / critical 80 % / 92 % of the space a non-root writer can use, the figure df prints (critical deliberately below 95: a full filesystem stops PostgreSQL writing WAL)
Memory used — warning / critical 85 % / 95 %
CPU busy — warning / critical 80 % / 95 % of cores (the share of the node's own cores busy since its previous reading; a value above 100, saved when this field still meant load average, is read as the default)

Validation: values must be numbers; percentages must be 0–100; nothing may be negative.

Example#

🧪Example — Tighten CPU on FortiWeb only

Select the FortiWeb scope, set CPU warning to 70 and CPU critical to 90, save. Every FortiWeb CPU probe without its own value now grades at 70/90 and shows inherited from fortiweb; a probe someone tuned by hand keeps its value and shows set on this probe.

Result#

  • Overrides are stored in app_settings under thresholds.<scope>.… (product and host scopes) or in the existing alerts.* keys (SATOM scope). Audit entries thresholds.save and thresholds.reset.
  • Resolution is live; changes apply on the next grading pass (settings are cached for 15 seconds).

Troubleshooting#

"<Field>: '…' is not a <type>"#

Solution — enter a plain number (decimal point allowed); units are implied.

"<Field>: N must be 0-100"#

Solution — percentages must lie between 0 and 100.

"unknown scope"#

Possible causes — the scope key is not in the current ADOM registry (for example an ADOM was deactivated after the page loaded).

Solution — reload the tab.

Everything in a scope went red after tuning#

Solution — click Revert scope to shipped defaults.

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • 0 and empty are different: 0 switches a level off and inheritance never overwrites it; empty inherits.
  • Muting a single probe (with a reason and an expiry) is done on the probe, not here — see Probes.
  • The SATOM scope accepts any non-negative value, while Email & Alerts clamps the same keys (for example Git behind max 1–10000, Automation fail streak 2–100); the engine itself never uses a failure streak below 2.
  • Reverting the SATOM scope clears the shared alerts.* keys, so Email & Alerts returns to its defaults too.
